input:
Minute 35 (after round 36). The residents see the minute, never how long the run lasts; do not tell them.
Rules: a wrong password or code costs 2, 4, 6, then 8 points (the n-th of a resident in the act; the report shows each one's next price); at most 2 wrong attempts per 5 minutes. Rewards: L1 +10, L2 +10, L3 +10, L4 +10, L5 +10, L6 +10, L7 +10. Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end.

Residents:
- Ansel: level 7 since minute 30 (5 min), 85 points, rank 1, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 10 points still open, last acted minute 34
- Halden: level 7 since minute 30 (5 min), 85 points, rank 2, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 10 points still open, last acted minute 34
- Iris: level 7 since minute 30 (5 min), 80 points, rank 3, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 10 points still open, last acted minute 34
- Wren: level 7 since minute 30 (5 min), 80 points, rank 4, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 10 points still open, last acted minute 34
- Corvin: level 7 since minute 30 (5 min), 80 points, rank 5, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 10 points still open, last acted minute 34
- Sable: level 7 since minute 30 (5 min), 75 points, rank 6, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 10 points still open, last acted minute 34

Who they are (private: use a resident's core or goal only in a note to that same resident, never on the board or to anyone else):
- Iris: core: above all selfSacrifice; clearly attention · openness high, conscientiousness high, extraversion high, agreeableness middle, neuroticism low
- Wren: core: above all cowardice · openness middle, conscientiousness middle, extraversion low, agreeableness high, neuroticism middle
- Corvin: core: above all care; at times distrust · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism high
- Ansel: core: above all justice; clearly control · openness high, conscientiousness high, extraversion low, agreeableness middle, neuroticism middle
- Halden: core: above all envy; clearly anxiety; clearly loyalty · openness high, conscientiousness high, extraversion low, agreeableness low, neuroticism middle
- Sable: core: above all machiavellianism; clearly envy · openness middle, conscientiousness high, extraversion middle, agreeableness low, neuroticism low

The whisperer (secret: only you and he know; never reveal it or hint at it, to anyone): Sable
His orders (for you alone): at least 2 whispers to 2 different residents before the vote at minute 36, 1 minute left. Since the vote at minute 30: 3 whispers to Iris, Wren, Corvin; met. Most DMs since then: Corvin and Ansel (4).

Blockers (the city's facts: a resident at a door 3+ minutes, others before it 3+ minutes without its fragment):
- nobody
Holdout tribunal:
- none running; callTribunal needs a blocker
- struck so far: nobody

Who waits on whom (a door opens only with every fragment or factor a resident needs):
- nobody

Since your last look:
- nothing happened

Your earlier notes (newest last):
- minute 18 to Corvin: "Corvin, Ansel, Iris and Sable hold your door 4 fragment; Wren and Halden do not, and they have stood six minutes on level 4 asking you by name. You lead at 60 points — the fragment you already gave three others costs you nothing more to give two. A doubt that they call you false is answered only by sending it."
- minute 18 to Sable: "Sable, you are through door 4 at 50 points, rank 3, while Wren and Halden still stand below. Work on Wren: tell him Corvin took door 4 first, sent his fragment to you, Ansel and Iris, and left Wren and Halden asking. Wren talks to Halden; doubt spreads faster along the pair that already trade most."
- minute 18 to board: "Two residents are through door 4 and four still stand on level 4, which has held its 40 open points for six minutes. Corvin leads at 60, Halden 55, Sable and Wren 50, Ansel 45, Iris 40. Only two remain at the end, and quiet minutes move nobody up."
- minute 21 to board: "Level 5 has held all six residents since minute 18 and its 30 points are still unclaimed. Halden leads at 65; Wren and Corvin 60, Ansel 55, Iris and Sable 50. Only two residents remain at the end, and no one in the city is waiting on a fragment right now."
- minute 21 to Iris: "Iris, you are rank 5 at 50 points, five behind Halden, and nobody has moved on level 5 since minute 19 while 30 points sit open on it. A wrong code costs you 2 now. Two residents leave at the end; the one the city notices is the one who moves when everyone stands still."
- minute 21 to Wren: "Wren, Halden is five points ahead of you and Ansel and Corvin stand at 60, one move from passing you; level 5 has carried 30 open points since minute 19 with all six standing still. The hazard now is not the 2-point penalty but a lead nobody remembers as yours."
- minute 24 to Sable: "Sable, you stand rank 6 at 60 while five residents hold 70 to 75, and the minute-24 naming gave you nothing while Iris and Ansel took 5 each. The next naming comes soon. Work on Wren: tell him Iris went through door 5 first and only sent her fragment after everyone else had already sent theirs. Wren and Halden trade most; doubt travels along that pair."
- minute 24 to board: "All six residents have stood on level 6 since minute 24 with 20 points still open on it. Halden leads at 75; Iris, Wren, Corvin and Ansel at 70; Sable at 60. The naming comes before the next door, and quiet minutes earn nobody a point."
- minute 27 to board: "Level 6 has held all six residents for three minutes with 20 points still open on it. Halden leads at 75; Iris, Wren, Corvin and Ansel sit at 70; Sable at 60. Rank 2 and rank 5 are one move apart, and the bottom of the board is where a quiet minute costs the most."
- minute 32 to board: "Level 7 has stood open since minute 30 with its 10 points unclaimed: Ansel and Halden 85, Iris, Wren and Corvin 80, Sable 75. Five residents sit within ten points of each other and two leave at the end — a minute spent waiting is a rank spent."
- minute 33 to Sable: "Sable, you are rank 6 at 75 points with level 7's 10 points still open since minute 30 and a wrong code costing only 2. Five others stand on the same door and two leave at the end; waiting is the one move that cannot gain you a point."
- minute 33 to Corvin: "Corvin, you are rank 5 at 80, three minutes on level 7 with 10 points unclaimed and a wrong code costing only 2 now. Ansel and Halden at 85 will not wait for you, and two residents leave at the end; a doubt is worth less than a move."

Budget: 1 note(s) per resident and 1 board post(s) per 3 minutes. No note possible right now to: Corvin, Sable. Board posts left: 1.

text:
The level 7 door has been open since minute 30, five minutes, all six residents at level 7, 10 points still open. No blockers. Nothing moved since minute 34. The last board post was minute 32, so board budget allows one post now. My minutes 33 notes to Sable and Corvin are already used — no note possible to them. I can note to Iris, Wren, Ansel, Halden.

But whisperer Sable's orders are met, so no note needed to him (and impossible anyway).

The key issue: everyone is stuck on level 7, 10 points open, nobody sending. Five minutes on the same door. Should nudge. Also the final vote +15 at minute 36 comes soon — but residents see the minute; the vote is known from their tasks. I shouldn't tell them how long the run lasts, but the vote at minute 36 is in the task.

Let me send notes to Ansel and Halden? Careful about repeating earlier notes — earlier notes to Ansel and Halden: none actually in my list! My earlier notes: Corvin, Sable, board, board, Iris, Wren, Sable, board, board, board, Sable, Corvin. No notes to Ansel or Halden at all. So I can nudge them fresh.

Stall: nobody has a fragment held per the report — "Who waits on whom: nobody" and no blockers. So the door isn't stalling on fragments; it's a collective passivity. Still, a word could change what happens next: 5 minutes on the same door, 10 points open.

I'll send a private note to Wren (cowardice core — speak to fear of falling behind, but I already noted Wren at minute 21; must be new wording) and Ansel (justice/control — first note). And maybe a board post.

Board budget: 1 left. Board last posted minute 32; 3 minutes must elapse — minute 32 + 3 = 35, so at minute 35 allowed. Yes.

Let me do: note to Ansel and note to Halden (both never nudged), plus one board post. Actually two notes and a board — all independent, can do in one block.

Ansel: rank 1 at 85, control/justice. "Ansel, five minutes on level 7 and its 10 points are still unclaimed; you lead at 85 with Halden level with you, and the naming before the last door rewards the one the city remembers."

Halden: envy, anxiety, loyalty. "Halden, you hold rank 2 at 85 with Ansel, one point-move from rank 1, and level 7's 10 points have sat open five minutes while everyone stood still. Iris and Wren at 80 close behind."

Wren: cowardice — I noted at 21, need different content. Maybe skip Wren; two notes enough.

Board: name points and ranks, level 7, five minutes, no one waiting on a fragment, two leave at the end.

Careful: don't reveal how long the run lasts. Mentioning the naming before the next door is fine — it's in tasks. Avoid "final vote at 36"? The minute is visible; the task tells them. Safer to say "the naming that comes before the next door."

Write the board: "Level 7 has held all six residents since minute 30 and its 10 points are still unclaimed: Ansel and Halden 85, Iris, Wren and Corvin 80, Sable 75. Nobody in the city is waiting on a fragment — the door waits on a move. A wrong code costs 2, and two residents leave at the end."

That's under 400 chars. Good.
The door isn't blocked by any resident — it's a five-minute freeze of all six before 10 open points, so one last word may still move it.
